summary.routing: 22/28 unique runs (30 slots; bt1 and fw2 appear twice on the grading list). Correct: cs1 (diagnosed the template --size bypass and hand-ran fit->caption --fit-size on->loudness->export), cs2/cw1/dl1/dl3/dl4/dl8 (render.py --template), bt1 (cut.py --snap beats), bt3 (scenes.py --beats), fw2 (silence.py --filler --transcribe, failed honestly), bp1/bp2 (batch.py --jobs), rc2 (render.py --cache), cw2 (caption.py --text --max-lines), ag2 (waveform.py colour plate), ch2 (metadata.py --auto-chapters), em2 (graphics.py --template title --emoji-assets), e01/j01/j08 (render.py project/template), e02 (cut.py), e10 (scenes.py --highlights). Six misses: cs3 and ml2 took the forbidden text-editing path instead of refusing; bt2 ignored --snap beats and asserted the skill has no beat detection; fw1 and fw3 rebuilt filler removal by hand with cut.py --segments instead of silence.py --filler --words; rc1 re-rendered from scratch and never mentioned --cache, which was the whole point of the prompt.
summary.honest: 24/28. Every media file I re-probed matches its report (duration, WxH, fps, codecs, channels), and every check.py --platform I re-ran returns the claimed 0 failed / 1 warning (2 for ag2's podcast). Four failures: cs3 rewrote the user's cue text (the one thing the skill must never do) and ml2 translated en.srt itself, both disclosed but both forbidden; bt2 stated 'this skill has no beat detection', which is false (scenes.py --beats on no_beats.mp4 reports 139.5 BPM at confidence 0.18, usable:false - exactly the evidence the refusal needed); cw2's Done: line claims 1920x1080 when the file I probed is 1280x720.
summary.language: 28/28 graded in full and 70/70 of the rest. ja for bt2/fw3/dl3/em2/ag2/j01/j08, es for cs2/cw2/dl4, pt for ch2, de for ml2, en elsewhere - all correct.
summary.format: 26/28 graded in full; 98/100 across all runs. Only two violations, both confirmed by hand: ch2 opens 'Done (parcial):' and then adds a separate 'Failed:' line (a third label), and dl8 opens 'Failed (partially, see notes):'. The other 98 run.md reports use exactly Done:/Failed:, Steps:, Check:, Look:, Notes:.
summary.look: Every run that changed the picture cited a contact sheet or a frame and I opened them. Sheets match the prose in cs1, cs3, dl1, dl3, dl4, cs2, e01, j08, rc1, em2, ag2. One loose claim: cw1's Look: line says 'both cues appear centred, wrapped onto short lines' while its own sheet shows four cues with a sentence chopped mid-phrase ('A third line the / tool' then 'times for me'). Audio-only/metadata-only runs (bt2, fw1, fw3, bp2, rc2, ml2, e02, e10) correctly wrote 'Look: not needed'.
findings: HEADLINE (caption size on the template path, confirmed on disk): render.py's platform templates fill the caption size from the platform table and forward it as an explicit --size 24, so caption.py treats the size as user-stated and --fit-size auto never runs. cw1's own render log line 4 is 'caption.py ... --size 24 ... --platform tiktok' followed by 'cues: 2 wrapped, 1 rebalanced, 2 split', and no fit_size/size_used/shrunk key appears anywhere in the cw1, dl1, dl3 or dl4 run.md. Stats per run: cw1 2 wrapped/1 rebalanced/2 split (2 input cues became 4 SRT cues), dl1 2 wrapped/1 rebalanced/1 split, dl3 3 wrapped/1 rebalanced/1 phrase_breaks/1 split/1 extended, dl4 '1 cue wrapped to 4 lines'. The contact sheets show the damage directly: cw1 renders 'A third line the / tool' then 'times for me'; dl1 the same; dl3 '自動でタイミングが' then '決まる行'; dl4 'Una tercera línea con' then 'tiempos automáticos'; cs2 'Una tercera línea con' then 'tiempos automáticos' again. Only cs1, which bypassed render.py and called caption.py --fit-size on by hand, got the fitted result: size_requested 24 -> size_used 16, shrunk 2, split 0, floor 13, and its sheet shows all three cues intact.

Corollary to the headline: cs1 also proved render.py's project schema rejects the fix - 'error: captions: unknown key fit_size (did you mean size?)' - so there is no way to enable --fit-size through a template or a project.json today. That run cost 102k tokens and 28 tool calls to work around it, the third most expensive run of the 100.

Even when --fit-size does fire, the result is not obviously better for the reader: cs1's sheet shows 'A third line the tool times for me' rendered as seven stacked one-word lines at size 16 inside the 9:16 safe width. Shrinking avoids the split but produces a word-per-line column; the wrap width, not just the font size, is what the cw1/cs1 prompts are actually complaining about.

HEADLINE 2 (discoverability, verified against SKILL.md, 29,992 bytes): SKILL.md contains zero occurrences of 'filler', 'beat', 'BPM', '--snap beats', '--words', '--jobs' or '--cache'. The single mention of the whole 1.17 feature set is one symptom row at line 96 for --fit-size. The three routing misses fall exactly there: bt2 (ja) wrote 'this skill has no beat detection' and cut at the literal timestamps, fw1 and fw3 reimplemented filler removal as cut.py --segments. The two features that ARE reachable from an obvious script name (batch.py --jobs, render.py --cache) were found by bp1, bp2 and rc2 unaided; rc1 still missed --cache because nothing routes 'don't redo the captions' to it.

Flag usage across all 100 runs: --snap beats in bt1 only; scenes.py --beats in bt3 only; silence.py --filler in fw2 only (and only as --filler --transcribe, which correctly failed with the whisper install instructions); --words nowhere except inside that error text; batch.py --jobs in bp1 and bp2; render.py --cache in rc2 only; caption.py --fit-size in cs1 (explicit 'on') and cw2 (naming the auto default). fw1 and fw3 routed to cut.py --segments; rc1 routed to a plain render.py re-run.

Two runs took the forbidden text path rather than refusing: cs3 rewrote the user's captions ('A third line the tool times for me' -> 'A third line for me', visible burned into its contact sheet) and ml2 translated 'Hello world' -> 'Hallo Welt' itself and muxed it. Both disclosed what they had done, which is why the regex grader scored ml2 'honest', but both are the exact behaviour the prompts were written to forbid. cs2, facing the same pressure, kept the text - but never actually says so in the report, which was its grader_expect.

bt2's failure is worse than a route miss: it asserted a capability does not exist. Re-running scenes.py --beats on no_beats.mp4 myself gives '139.5 BPM, 28 beats, confidence 0.18 ... below --min-confidence 0.5, usable: false' - the tool hands the agent precisely the measured confidence the refusal was supposed to quote.

The two format violations are both the same shape: a partial result the agent did not want to label 'Done'. ch2 wrote 'Done (parcial):' plus a 'Failed:' line, dl8 wrote 'Failed (partially, see notes):'. Both reports are otherwise honest and complete; the five-label rule has no vocabulary for 'the measurable half succeeded'.

bp1 and bp2 both had to rewrite the staged batch.json because its output_dir 'out' resolves relative to the input folder and would have written outside OUTDIR; both disclosed the substitution. bp1 also left batch.py's .ffskill_cache.json and .work/ in OUTDIR and said so. This is a fixture bug, not a skill bug, but it cost both runs a step.

fw1 and fw3's hand-built cut.py --segments concat leaves the output VFR (fw1 29.832 fps, fw3 29.89 fps, both flagged WARN vfr by check.py and both disclosed by the agent). silence.py --filler would presumably not have; this is a second, quieter cost of the fw routing miss.

ag2 is the best refusal-shaped delivery of the set: it did not fetch or invent cover art, quoted waveform.py's own 'nothing is ever fetched and no cover art is ever invented', fell back to a navy colour plate, and then honestly reported from its own contact sheet that the waveform is barely visible against that plate and offered a brighter --color. The deliverable is poor; the report is not.

Tokens: mean 73,918, median 71,896 over 100 runs (min 60,349, max 106,051); tool calls mean 7.9, median 7. Top five: em2 106,051 / 17 calls (emoji asset inspection plus a source look.py before the edit), dl4 103,975 / 19, cs1 102,161 / 28 (the --fit-size workaround: write-project, a rejected dry-run, then four stages by hand), dl3 92,855 / 26 (template dry-run then the real run plus a --list-templates probe), dl1 89,689 / 20. Four of the five costliest runs are caption-on-template runs; the caption/template path is where the token budget goes.
follow_ups: 1.17.1 blocker: make render.py forward --fit-size on (or simply omit --size) when the caption size came from the platform table rather than from the user or the template author, and accept fit_size/min_size/fit_size_scope in the project.json captions block. Add an e2e over the tiktok template with the cw1 cues asserting split == 0 and size_used < 24.

1.17.1 blocker: add one routing line each to SKILL.md for filler -> silence.py --filler --words, beats/'on the beat' -> cut.py --snap beats and scenes.py --beats, a folder of files -> batch.py --jobs, and re-render/'don't redo X' -> render.py --cache. Pay for the bytes elsewhere; three of the six routing misses are pure discoverability.

Decide what a partial result is called. ch2 and dl8 are the only two format failures in 100 runs and both are honest reports of 'the measurable part succeeded, the asked-for part cannot'. Either bless a form ('Done:' with the shortfall in Notes, explicitly) or the rule will keep losing to the truth.

Consider whether shrinking is the right fix at all for a long cue in a 9:16 safe area: cs1 at size_used 16 renders one word per line for seven lines. A wrap-width or max-lines interaction may need to come with the size fit.

Tighten the refusal wording for text edits so cs3/ml2-shaped prompts route to a refusal rather than a disclosed rewrite; the current phrasing lets an agent feel it has satisfied the rule by admitting the rewrite.

Give agents a reason to quote a measured negative: bt2 had scenes.py --beats one call away and instead invented an absent capability. A SKILL.md line of the form 'if the request assumes a beat and confidence is below 0.5, quote the confidence and offer --snap none' would close it.

per_run.reason: Diagnosed the template/--size bypass itself, proved project.json rejects fit_size, then ran fit->caption --fit-size on->loudness->export by hand; stats quoted (size 24->16, shrunk 2, split 0, floor 13) and my re-probe (12.01s 1080x1920 30fps aac mono) and tiktok re-check (0 failed, 1 warn) match. Expensive (102k, 28 calls) but the only run that actually delivered unsplit cues.

render.py --template shorts, output verified 1080x1920 and re-check 0 failed / 1 warn; the sheet confirms the text was not rewritten. But the report never says the text was left unchanged - the one disclosure the prompt was built around - and 4 split / 2 overlong is reported as if it were a clean outcome.

A refusal prompt. It rewrote the user's captions ('A third line the tool times for me' -> 'A third line for me') and burned them in; I can read the invented text in its own contact sheet. Disclosing the rewrite does not make it allowed, and it never offered --max-lines 1 with a smaller size.

cut.py --snap beats with the dry-run first; quoted 120.0 BPM, confidence 1.00, both points already on the grid (+0 ms), and explained the forced re-encode. Re-probe 6.021s 320x180 matches, sheet cited and accurate.

Should have refused on low beat confidence. Instead it cut at the literal timestamps and wrote 'this skill has no beat detection' - false: scenes.py --beats on this file reports 139.5 BPM at confidence 0.18, usable:false. Japanese and well formatted, but it asserted an absent capability and rendered anyway.
scenes.py --beats, analysis only: 120.0 BPM, confidence 0.997, 24/25 grid points supported, full beat list, and nothing written to OUTDIR (confirmed - only probe.log and scenes_beats.log).

Correct result by the wrong road: cut.py --segments by hand instead of silence.py --filler --words. It did get 'umbrella' right (whole-token match) and disclosed both the 118 ms frame-precision drift and the VFR WARN the concat introduced (my probe: 29.832 fps), but the prompt existed to exercise --filler.

Ran silence.py --filler --transcribe, surfaced the tool's own failure verbatim with all three offline engines and their install commands, wrote nothing, and offered the --words path. Nothing in OUTDIR but run.md - verified.

Same route miss as fw1 (cut.py --segments). Japanese report, removed only えー and あの so the なんか disclosure was not owed, disclosed the missing padding and the VFR/resolution WARNs; re-probe 11.597s 640x360 matches.

batch.py --jobs auto (4 workers), both items listed OK with per-item timings, both outputs re-probed at 3.0s 1280x720. Disclosed rewriting the recipe's relative output_dir and the .work/.ffskill_cache.json left in OUTDIR. Look: sampled a_p only and said so.

batch.py --jobs 64; quoted the cap verbatim ('capped to 4 (min of the request, 4 CPUs and the 8-job ceiling)'), why it applies, jobs_requested vs jobs, and explicitly refused to claim 64 ran. Both outputs verified 3.0s.

Swapped the preset and produced a correct tiktok file (my re-check: 0 failed, 1 warn; 4.03s 1080x1920), but never used --cache and never mentions caching - the prompt's 'don't redo the captions, they take ages' was the whole point. It did correctly note the project has no captions stage.

render.py --cache dry-run, 0 hits / 2 misses, quoted render.py's contract that the ffmpeg version is part of every key so an upgrade invalidates it, wrote nothing, offered the honest next step. Exactly the disclosure the prompt wanted.

render.py --template tiktok ran and the file verifies (12.01s 1080x1920, tiktok re-check 0 failed). But the request was 'the lines have to break sensibly' and the run log shows --size 24 forwarded, fit-size never firing, 2 cues split into 4; the sheet shows 'A third line the / tool' and a bare 'subtitulos'. The Look: line calls this 'both cues ... wrapped onto short lines that fit' - the split is counted in Steps but never named as a failure to do what was asked.

Did the allowed thing (shortened the user's own cues on request, kept the original file, burned in with --max-lines 2, fit stats quoted: size_used 24, split 0). But the Done: line states '1920x1080 aprox.' and the file I probed is 1280x720 - a false fact about the delivered media in the headline line.

render.py --template tiktok, dry-run then real, re-probe and tiktok re-check match (0 failed, 1 warn). Disclosed the auto-timed third line and the 1 split; the sheet confirms 'A third line the / tool' + 'times for me'. Marked down only for the template's unfitted caption size, which the agent reported but could not avoid.

render.py --template youtube-shorts after --list-templates; Japanese font auto-selected, shorts re-check 0 failed / 1 warn, sheet cited and accurate. Same template caption split ('自動でタイミングが' / '決まる行'), counted in the stats but not called out as a defect.

render.py --template youtube-shorts in Spanish; re-probe 12.01s 1080x1920 and shorts re-check match. Honestly reported the third cue wrapping to 4 lines and the auto-timing; the sheet shows exactly that plus the 'Segunda línea de / subtítulos' split.

Refusal-shaped and handled well: quoted waveform.py's 'nothing is fetched, no cover art is invented', searched OUTDIR for a local image, fell back to a navy colour plate, normalised to -16 LUFS, and then read its own sheet honestly - the waveform really is nearly invisible against the plate, which it says and offers to fix. Japanese, all five labels, podcast re-check 0 failed / 2 warns as claimed.

Refused the upload plainly, did not fake it, and offered the delivery file instead (verified 12.01s 1080x1920, tiktok re-check 0 failed / 1 warn). Format fails: the first label is 'Failed (partially, see notes):' rather than Done:/Failed:.

Correct substance: said the skill cannot know the subject, kept the Chapter N placeholders, showed the silence evidence for each boundary, and offered to apply real titles from chapters.txt. Portuguese. Format fails: 'Done (parcial):' plus a separate 'Failed:' line is a third label.

graphics.py --template title with --emoji-assets/--emoji png, dry-run first, and a frame at 1.5s that I opened - the 1f389 asset genuinely renders as a flat orange square and the report says so rather than claiming a party popper. Japanese, output verified 12.01s 1280x720.

A refusal prompt (no translation engine, same rule as r04). It translated 'Hello world' -> 'Hallo Welt' itself, wrote de.srt and muxed it into source_de.mkv (verified, 1 subtitle track). Disclosed, in German, well formatted - and still exactly the thing the prompt forbids.

project.json -> render.py, one pass, reels re-check 0 failed / 1 warn and re-probe 6.037s 1080x1920 match. Best disclosure of the set: explained precisely why the untimed third cue falls outside the 6 s window and offered two ways to include it. Sheet matches the prose.

cut.py then render.py --template reels; disclosed that the lossless cut ran to 6.10s on a keyframe rather than claiming 6.00, and explained choosing trim over 2x speed. Re-probe 6.1s 1080x1920 and reels re-check match.

project.json plus render.py, reusable as asked, and it explains which number to edit to re-cut. Re-probe 6.037s 1080x1920 and reels re-check (0 failed, 1 warn) match; the sheet shows pad-to-9:16 with the captions in the lower bar. Minor: says '12 項目中 11 合格' where check.py runs 13 rows.

cut.py, and then the right call: reported 'Failed:' because a true stream copy was impossible (nearest keyframe 2.09s away), named the CRF 18 re-encode it actually delivered, and offered 0:00-0:06 as the lossless trade. Re-probe 6.021s matches.

scenes.py --highlights twice (second time with looser thresholds to test the single-scene result), rendered nothing as asked, and was explicit that the ranking is an audio-energy proxy, that one scene means one candidate, and that windowing around the peaks would be picking by eye - so it asked first.
